findings.failure_path: _live_syntax resets quote state for each line. A Python heredoc containing example = """ followed by open('hooks/gate.py', 'w') on the next line and closing triple quotes only constructs a string, yet the middle line produces a shared target and can spend the checkpoint. Conversely, matching each line separately stops recognizing executable open(\n'hooks/gate.py', 'w'), which the previous whole-code regex recognized.
findings.smallest_fix: Use whole-code, interpreter-aware tokenization for string/comment exclusion while preserving multiline call matching; conservatively skip unsupported syntax. Add fresh-context controls for multiline strings and a positive multiline-call regression.

findings.failure_path: MAX_TARGETS is checked only before dispatching a segment. A command below 64 KiB containing touch followed by 1,000 distinct hooks/*.py operands resolves and returns all 1,000 targets in one _segment call. The claimed 256-target work bound therefore does not exist, undermining the resource-containment fix.
findings.smallest_fix: Enforce a shared remaining-work budget before each target resolution, including inline-code and nested-shell extraction. Add a single-command many-operands test that asserts the resolution bound, not merely a truncated result.
